lesson.title: Reading the Mean Value Theorem's Conclusion
lesson.summary: The equation f'(c) = [f(b)-f(a)]/(b-a) is the heart of the Mean Value Theorem. Read geometrically, it says the tangent line at some point c is parallel to the secant line joining the two endpoints, and that point can usually be pinned down exactly.
lesson.body:
Once the hypotheses of continuity and differentiability are confirmed, the entire content of the Mean Value Theorem lives in one equation: f'(c) = [f(b) - f(a)] / (b - a) for some c in (a,b). The right side is a single fixed number for a given function and interval, the average rate of change, so the equation is really asking for which x does the instantaneous rate of change f'(x) equal this specific number. Solving that equation for x and then keeping only the solutions that land inside the open interval (a,b) is the standard procedure for actually finding c.

Geometrically, [f(b)-f(a)]/(b-a) is the slope of the secant line through the two points (a, f(a)) and (b, f(b)) on the graph of f. The equation f'(c) equal to that same number says the tangent line to the curve at x = c has that exact slope too, so the tangent line at c is parallel to the secant line connecting the endpoints. Visually, if you took the secant line and slid it, without rotating it, from one side of the graph to the other, there is a moment where it becomes tangent to the curve, touching it at exactly one point c, rather than cutting through it at two.

Work this out for f(x) = sqrt(x) on the interval [1, 4]. As a square root function, f is continuous on [1,4] and differentiable on (1,4), since 1 is greater than 0 keeps everything away from the domain trouble at 0, so the theorem applies. The endpoint values are f(1) = sqrt(1) = 1 and f(4) = sqrt(4) = 2, so the secant line's slope, the average rate of change, is (2-1)/(4-1) = 1/3. The derivative is f'(x) = 1/(2 sqrt(x)), so the conclusion asks for c with 1/(2 sqrt(c)) = 1/3. Cross multiplying, 2 sqrt(c) = 3, so sqrt(c) = 3/2, and c = 9/4 = 2.25. Since 1 is less than 2.25 which is less than 4, this c lies in the open interval as required. Checking directly, f'(9/4) = 1/(2 times 1.5) = 1/3, which matches the average rate exactly, confirming that at x = 2.25 the tangent line to the square root curve is exactly parallel to the secant line running from (1,1) to (4,2).

This solve for c, then check it lands in (a,b) pattern is the practical skill the conclusion equation is really for. It shows up throughout the applications ahead, whenever the goal shifts from proving a point c exists in principle to actually locating it or reasoning about what its existence implies.
